headline: n8n can write and execute server-side workflows while Superset can call APIs, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no critical compliance issue is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow content and execute server-side code, and Superset exposes an API surface that could carry attacker-controlled text into n8n-managed workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation between outputs and inputs, so prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. This is more than manual copy-paste, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Superset API responses are routed into n8n AI Agent nodes without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF n8n workflows parse Superset-generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer execution.
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist filter before any Superset text reaches n8n AI nodes.
Insert a human review step for any workflow that turns API text into instructions.
Prefix all machine-generated content with non-executable delimiters.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags through the workflow chain.
requires-engineering: separate untrusted content into a non-agent processing lane.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress, server filesystem access, and handles per-credential secrets; Superset can call its API and may receive workflow outputs. If shared data includes sensitive workflow content, n8n can move it outward through integrations. Superset itself is not shown to exfiltrate by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF sensitive workflow data is processed by n8n and then sent through an integration node, leakage occurs.
IF Superset consumes n8n outputs containing secrets or personal data, those data enter another system boundary.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any workflow payload before it reaches n8n integrations.
Use a test dataset instead of production records for shared workflows.
Restrict n8n credentials to the minimum required integration nodes.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction on workflow outputs.
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive workflows onto a separate n8n instance.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and execute shell commands, while Superset exposes an API and can also receive API-driven updates. Even without explicit git overlap, both agents can mutate shared backend resources if pointed at the same systems, creating write contention and inconsistent state. Uncertainty about the exact shared resources pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same database, filesystem, or API-backed resource, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF n8n workflows invoke shell or file writes against resources Superset also updates, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts for each agent.
Point each agent at distinct working directories.
Disable shell/file-write steps in workflows that do not need them.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: introduce optimistic concurrency checks on shared records.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate downstream actions from AI Agent nodes, and Superset can supply API-fed data that n8n may treat as workflow input. If n8n treats Superset output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions or reports. The pair is not proven to auto-act by default, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF n8n uses Superset output as a decision input without verification, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF a workflow converts Superset data into automated actions, a bad upstream value can trigger incorrect actions.
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action-taking node.
Require schema validation on all Superset-derived inputs.
Log and review a sample of automated decisions daily.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before execution.
requires-engineering: separate read-only analytics from action-taking workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is evidenced in either profile. n8n handles whatever the workflow processes, while Superset has no declared sensitive-data classes or compliance constraints here. Because the profiles are sparse and the rubric says uncertainty escalates, I avoid none but keep this low rather than inventing a breach.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data and routes it into a noncompliant deployment, a compliance issue may arise.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed externally, the pair may need additional controls.
mitigations: Document the data classes each workflow handles.
Confirm retention settings for both systems.
Avoid regulated data in shared workflows until controls are reviewed.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention policies end to end.
requires-engineering: add compliance gates before exporting data.
